'''Towatari Shrine''' (登渡神社, ''Towatari-jinja''), also known as '''Nobuto Shrine''' (登戸神社, ''Nobuto-jinja''), is a [[Shinto]] {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in Nobuto, {{ill|Chūō-ku, Chiba|en|Chūō-ku, Chiba|qid=Q1075869|lt=Chūō-ku}}, {{ill|Chiba (city)|en|Chiba (city)|qid=Q170616|lt=Chiba City}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|en|Chiba Prefecture|qid=Q80011|lt=Chiba Prefecture}}, Japan. Originally a branch {{ill|Buddhist temples in Japan|en|Buddhist temples in Japan|qid=Q3141900|lt=temple}} of Kongojū-ji, a temple to the {{ill|Buddhism in Japan|en|Buddhism in Japan|qid=Q736311|lt=Buddhist}} {{ill|Deva (Buddhism)|en|Deva (Buddhism)|qid=Q4089509|lt=deity}} {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken}} founded by the [[Chiba clan]] (modern [[Chiba Shrine]]), it was converted into a Shinto shrine during the mid-19th century.

==Deities==
The shrine is dedicated to the three deities of creation (造化三神, ''zōka sanshin'') of classical [[Japanese mythology]]: [[Ame-no-Minakanushi]], [[Takamimusubi]], and [[Kamimusubi]]. Enshrined together with them is [[:ja:天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|Ame-no-Hiwashi]], originally the deity of a nearby shrine that was [[Shrine Consolidation Policy|merged]] into Nobuto Shrine in 1908 ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji}} 41).<ref name="history2">{{cite web|title=登渡神社について|url=https://www.towatarijinjya.com/jinjya|accessdate=2020-11-16|website=Towatari Shrine Official Website|language=Japanese}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Bay of Noboto.jpg|left|thumb|270x270px|''Bay of Noboto'' (Nobuto) by [[:en:Katsushika Hokusai|Katsushika Hokusai]]]]
The shrine was originally founded in 1644 ({{ill|Shōhō|en|Shōhō|qid=Q1146192|lt=Shōhō}} 1) by [[:ja:千葉定胤|Chiba Sadatane]], 33rd head of the [[Chiba clan]], as a Buddhist temple named '''Hakujasan Shinkō-in Jōin-ji''' (白蛇山真光院定胤寺). It was a branch temple or ''matsuji'' (末寺) of Kongojū-ji (also known as Chiba Myōken-ji), a temple dedicated to {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken}}, the Buddhist deification of the {{ill|Big Dipper|en|Big Dipper|qid=Q10460|lt=Big Dipper}} and/or the {{ill|Polaris|en|Polaris|qid=Q12980|lt=northern pole star}} revered by the Chiba clan as their patron deity (what is today [[Chiba Shrine]]).<ref name="history2" /><ref>{{cite book |editor=Chiba Prefecture |title=千葉県誌 巻上 (Chiba-ken shi, vol. 1) |date=1919 |publisher=Tadaya Shoten |pages=521 |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/960652/297}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Nozaki |first1=Sabun |title=日本名勝地誌 第二編 (Nihon meishōchi shi, vol. 2) |date=1901 |publisher=Hakubunkan |page=166 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PkxMpcnBkZQC&dq=%E7%99%BB%E6%B8%A1%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE&pg=PP200}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=登渡神社 (Towatari-jinja) |url=http://www.jinja.ne.jp/ycDB/Board.cgi/001/db/ycDB-pc-jinja_detail.html?mode:search=1&search:method=1&search:field=jinja_id&search:expr=^$&search:word=1008 |website=神社のひろば 神社探検隊！ |publisher=Chiba-ken Jinjachō |accessdate=2020-11-18|language=Japanese}}</ref>

In 1867 ({{ill|Keiō|en|Keiō|qid=Q776775|lt=Keiō}} 3), the temple became a Shinto shrine dedicated to the [[Kami|gods]] [[Ame-no-Minakanushi]] (a deity in Japanese mythology conflated with Myōken), [[Takamimusubi]], and [[Kamimusubi]] and renamed "Towatari Shrine".<ref name="history2" />

In 1990 ([[:en:Heisei|Heisei]] 2), the shrine's ''[[honden]]'' (dating from 1860) was moved to its present location and a new [[Heiden (Shinto)|''hei'']]-''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'' constructed in front of it.<ref name="history2" />

==Structures==
*'''''Honden'''''
:The ''honden'' was originally Jōin-ji's former {{ill|Main Hall (Japanese Buddhism)|en|Main Hall (Japanese Buddhism)|qid=Q17051413|lt=main hall}}, constructed in 1860 by a craftsman named Monjirō (紋次郎) from the [[:ja:八木村 (千葉県)|village of Yagi]] in [[:ja:葛飾郡|Katsushika District]], {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|qid=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}} (part of the modern city of {{ill|Nagareyama|en|Nagareyama|qid=Q328625|lt=Nagareyama}}, Chiba Prefecture).{{efn|Other notable projects by this artisan include the former main hall (the current Shaka-dō (釈迦堂) or Hall of [[:en:Gautama Buddha|Shakyamuni Tathāgata]]) of {{ill|Narita-san|en|Narita-san|qid=Q3083875|lt=Shinshō-ji}} in {{ill|Narita, Chiba|en|Narita, Chiba|qid=Q273798|lt=Narita}} (built 1858)<ref>{{cite book |author1=Shiritsu Narita Toshokan |title=成田山通志 (Narita-san Tsushi) |date=1911 |publisher=Shiritsu Narita Toshokan |page=76 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QgNjpoXOSZMC}}</ref> and the former main hall of [[:ja:深川不動堂|Fukagawa Fudō-dō]] (a branch of Shinshō-ji) in {{ill|Fukagawa, Tokyo|en|Fukagawa, Tokyo|qid=Q3090689|lt=Fukagawa}}, {{ill|Kōtō|en|Kōtō|qid=Q215175|lt=Kōtō City}}, {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo}} - originally a sanctuary dedicated to the {{ill|Bodhisattva|en|Bodhisattva|qid=Q178149|lt=Bodhisattva}} {{ill|Kṣitigarbha|en|Kṣitigarbha|qid=Q604687|lt=Kṣitigarbha}} (地蔵堂, Jizō-dō) in [[:ja:|Ryūfuku-ji]] in what is now [[:en:Inzai, Chiba|Inzai]] built somewhere between 1861 and 1864<ref>{{cite web |title=深川不動堂旧本堂 |url=https://www.city.koto.lg.jp/103020/bunkasports/bunka/bunkazaisiseki/kenzobutsu/17348.html |website=Kōtō City Official Website |language=Japanese}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=今むかし④～本堂移築 |url=http://fukagawafudou.jugem.jp/?eid=314 |website=Narita-san Fukagawa Fudō-dō |accessdate=2020-11-18 |language=Japanese}}</ref>.}}<ref name="history2" /><ref>{{cite book |editor=Chiba-shi Shi Hensan Iinkai |title=千葉市誌 (Chiba-shi Shi) |date=1958 |publisher=Chiba-shi Shi Hensan Iinkai |page=175}}</ref> The bas-reliefs decorating the building were carved by [[:ja:立川和四郎|Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa]] (立川和四郎富昌, the 2nd generation of the Tatekawa Washirō line of craftsmen) from Suwa District in {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}} (modern {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}) and/or his son Tomishige (富重).<ref name="history2" /><ref name="towatari-reliefs">{{cite web |title=小壁嵌板彫刻（市指定文化財） |url=https://www.city.chiba.jp/kyoiku/shogaigakushu/bunkazai/kokabehameita.html |website=Chiba City Official Website |accessdate=2020-11-18 |language=Japanese}}</ref> The reliefs were designated [[Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|tangible cultural properties]] by Chiba City in 1967 ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}} 42).<ref name="towatari-reliefs"/>
